extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news publishers, media researchers, policymakers and students interested in global news consumption
extracted.subtask_description: A global, cross‑country research report measuring how people consume news (platforms, trust, engagement, subscriptions, avoidance, attitudes to AI and personalisation) and how publishers might respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform of news consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures where people access news (social media, video platforms, print, podcasts, AI chatbots, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report emphasises 'an accelerating shift towards consumption via social media and video platforms.' Example figures on the page: only 10% in Brazil say they access news on print (down from 50% in 2013), podcasts (10%) and AI chatbots (9%). Country differences are highlighted and the interactive allows comparison by market and demographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with traditional news media
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments of how well traditional news media connect with the public, including measures of engagement over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overview notes 'traditional news media struggling to connect with much of the public, with declining engagement.' Use longitudinal measures of readership, web traffic, broadcast audience and other engagement indicators to capture trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels of public trust in news organisations and news generally, reported by country and market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page flags 'low trust' and names countries with lowest trust in the sample (e.g., Hungary and Greece both 22%). Trust should be measured and compared across countries and over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital subscriptions and willingness to pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of paid news consumption: subscriptions, who is paying for online news, and subscription trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary refers to 'stagnating digital subscriptions' and includes a podcast 'Who's paying for online news?' — track subscription growth/decline and demographic patterns of payers.

rubrics_metrics.name: News avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which people avoid news and the proportion of the population engaged in avoidance behaviours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights show high avoidance in some countries (Bulgaria 63%, Croatia 61%). Use survey measures to capture reasons for avoidance and cross‑country comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform‑specific usage (e.g., TikTok, X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of news use on specific platforms such as TikTok and X (formerly Twitter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights country differences: Thailand (49%), Malaysia (48%), Kenya (40%) have highest TikTok news use. It also poses platform questions like 'Do people still use X for news?'. Measure platform penetration and news consumption behaviour by platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI tools (AI chatbots and attitudes to AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which people use AI chatbots for news and their attitudes toward AI in news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives a figure for AI chatbot use (9%) and includes a podcast 'Attitudes to AI in news | Digital News Report 2025'. Track both behavioural use and normative/attitudinal measures toward AI in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the public checks information they think might be wrong (verification behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience practices for verifying or checking potentially incorrect information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a feature ('How the public checks information it thinks might be wrong' by Rasmus Nielsen). Capture behaviours, preferred verification sources and steps audiences take when they suspect misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of misinformation (concerned sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which sources of misinformation people find most concerning and the perceived credibility of misinformation vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site includes content 'The most concerning sources of misinformation' and multimedia exploring this; measure perceived threat from different misinformation sources and platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local publishers' value to audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: How local news organisations can provide value and the audience needs they fulfil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A feature 'How local publishers can provide value to audiences' by Richard Fletcher suggests evaluating local relevance, trust, and service to communities as metrics of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: News personalisation and audience attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience opinions about news personalisation, especially in the context of AI-driven recommendation or tailoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 'How audiences think about news personalisation in the age of AI' indicates the report measures attitudes toward personalisation tradeoffs (relevance vs filter bubble/privacy). Include attitudinal and behavioural measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: News podcasts landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics and changing patterns in news podcast consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report contains 'The changing landscape of news podcasts' — measure podcast usage, demographics, formats, and trends over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications strategy and overload
rubrics_metrics.description: How publishers use notifications to engage audiences while avoiding overload and user fatigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature 'Walking the notification tightrope: How to engage audiences while avoiding overload' by Nic Newman — metrics should include opt‑in rates, open/click rates, and audience sentiment about notification frequency and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country and market comparative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross‑country and market breakdowns of all measures (platforms, trust, subscriptions, avoidance, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides lists of countries and 'Explore data from your country' interactive; the report is explicitly comparative and interactive charts enable market/demographic comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear description of how research was conducted (sampling, survey instruments, fieldwork periods, definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to 'Methodology' ('How we conducted our research for the Digital News Report 2025.'). Although details are on the methodology page, the report signals the importance of documenting methods for interpreting metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse and attribution policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reusing and attributing the report's materials (videos, slides, audio) within other websites and presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site states 'We encourage free, attributed reuse of our work within your own websites and presentations.' This is a production/use guideline rather than a measurement metric; include licensing/attribution practices when reusing content.
